conventions: All strings are real Unicode characters (the C++ \x.. UTF-8 escapes are decoded). All indices and lengths count Unicode code points; every string here is in the BMP, so they equal the UTF-16 offsets of the Fushi tests. "variants": text_processor::process(input); languages "all" means every preprocessor chain is enabled, in Fushi's order Japanese (NFKC, kana conversion, emphatic collapse, ASCII to full width, kanji variants, iteration marks, full-width digits to kanji numerals), English (apostrophes, lowercase), diacritics (combining marks/harakat/Hebrew points, precomposed Latin-1 letters), Korean jamo disassembly last. Every string in "present" must be among the deduplicated variants and none in "absent"; "steps", when given, maps a variant to its minimal step count. "candidates": scan_candidates(input, scan_length) returns the prefixes of the first scan_length code points, longest first, never cutting between two letters of space-delimited scripts and dropping prefixes that end in whitespace; "expected" is the exact ordered list ("present"/"absent" when the test checks membership only). "hangul": disassemble turns precomposed syllables and complex compatibility jamo into simple compatibility jamo (ㅘ -> ㅗㅏ, ㄺ -> ㄹㄱ); reassemble composes them back, a consonant followed by a vowel starting a new syllable; other characters pass through. "query" (LKP-001/LKP-002): the string looked up after a click on code point "click" of "text". "cue": text is the whole cue and the query may run to its end; "free": at most 400 characters from the start point. If the clicked character belongs to a script written with spaces, the start point moves back while the preceding character is neither whitespace nor a delimiter, so the back-off stops at apostrophes (l’homme clicked in homme gives homme); Fushi backs off for every character outside its JAPANESE_RANGES (kana, CJK ideographs, U+3000-U+303F, half/full-width forms), and no case here depends on the difference. The scan then stops at the first delimiter of 。、！？…‥「」『』（）()【】〈〉《》〔〕｛｝{}［］[]・：；:;，,.─\n\r"'“”‘’«»‹›, except an intra-word apostrophe: ' U+0027, ‘ U+2018, ’ U+2019 or ʼ U+02BC (not a delimiter anyway) with a letter of a space-delimited script immediately on both sides (the same letter set as candidates: Fushi word_scan.cpp is_space_delimited_letter; digits, tatweel, Thai and CJK are not letters). A whitespace character is crossed only if it is not at the start point and the next character exists and is neither whitespace nor a delimiter, so the query never ends in whitespace. "sentence" (T-TXT-007): Fushi extractSentenceAt over a flat string; click is the selection start and options.sel_len its length. The sentence starts after the nearest 。！？.!?\n\r before click and ends at the first one at or after click + sel_len, inclusive, plus any directly following closers 。、！？…‥」』）)】〉》〕｝}］], and is trimmed; out-of-range selections are clamped; sel_len 0 or 1 gives the same sentence in every case here. "expected_selection", when present, is the selection re-based into the trimmed sentence (start, length). "divergence" marks a case where Nikomiru's requirement differs from Fushi: "expected" follows the requirement and fushi_expected is Fushi's value. "skip" marks a test that cannot be expressed (source-level guards, dictionary lookups, DOM-only operations); its fields are placeholders unless the note says otherwise. Query and sentence cases translated from Fushi's JS harnesses name the Dart test, the harness file and the assertion marker; Fushi asserts every q2056-* case against both of its selection engines (popup/extension selection.js and the reader script), the q3453-* cases against the reader script only.
